sentences.text: This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 01.02.2023 at about 8.15 p.m, when the Petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KA-8163 from new BEL towards Ashwathanagar junction on the left side of SCCH 15 3 MVC No.886/2023 80 feet road and when he reached near Trafal Restaurant, Sanjayanagara, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 who parked the said car suddenly took U turn without observing the vehicle movements in a rash and negligently, in this process accident had occurred.
Due to which, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Ramaiah Memorial Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

He had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was running Tailoring shop and was earning 50,000/- per month.
On account of accidental injuries he cannot do his work.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 by its driver.

The Respondent SCCH 15 4 MVC No.886/2023 No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement contended that the Petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, it has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.886/2023 conditions of the policy.

Further it contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and the Petitioner without having proper look out vehicular movements on the road,
ridden his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 01.02.2023 at about 8.15 p.m., on 80 feet road,
near Trafal Restaurant, Sanjayanagara, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024?
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.886/2023 2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable?

3 . What Order or Award?
7.

Further, he examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 9 documents at Ex.14 to 20 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.

8. During the course of Arguments, The learned counsel for the Petitioner has relied on the following decisions:

Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and the decisions relied on and the materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 SCCH 15 8 MVC No.886/2023  Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 by its driver.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 by its driver.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-13 and he has re-iterated the Petition averments in his Chief-affidavit.
Ex . P-1

to Ex.P-13 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar and Sketch,
Police Notice with Reply, IMV report, Wound Certificate, Charge sheet, Medical bills, advance receipts, Payment receipts, Aadhar card and PAN card.
SCCH 15 9 MVC No.886/2023 12.

Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P- 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the Petitioner himself, the R.T. Nagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of Spot Mahazar with Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 and 5 are the Police Notice and Reply.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P.8 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the ASI, R.T. Nagar Traffic Police Station against the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

14 . P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.
Further the Petitioner has examined MRT of Ramaiah Hospital by name Shankar as PW.2 and got marked five documents at Ex.P14 to 18.
Further he has examined Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW.3 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P19 and 20.
PW.3 has reiterated the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by the Petitioner.

To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 has examined its Manager - Legal by name Santhosh as RW.1 and he has reiterated the Objection Statement contentions in his SCCH 15 11 MVC No.886/2023 chief-affidavit and also got marked Authorization letter and copy of Police at Ex.R1 and 2.
15.

It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that the Respondent No.1 had driven the car without valid DL and has contravened the provisions of MV Act and thereby committed the brach of terms and conditions of the policy.
However, in the cross-examination RW.1, he has admitted that the FIR and Charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
He further admitted that as per Ex.P3 i.e., Spot sketch and Mahazar, car after taking U turn accident occurred to the motorcycle.
Upon going through Ex.P3 Sketch and Spot mahazar which clearly exhibited that the car had taken U turn towards its right side and the accident was caused to the motorcycle.
Further the RW.1 denied the suggestions that Ex.P5 shows that the person who holds DL was sat by the side of the driver of the car.

But, upon going through Ex.P5 i.e., Reply given by the owner of the offending vehicle in response to the Police Notice shows the name of the driver as M.N Anjan SCCH 15 12 MVC No.886/2023 But, very next it shows the DL holder as Apoorva N.M.
Further it shows that the driver of the offending vehicle holds LLR which is valid from 14.11.2022 to 13.06.2023.

Added to it,
the Respondent No.2 has also examined the FDA, RTO of KR Puram, Bengaluru by name Nagaraj as RW.2 and he got marked Authorization letter and Certified copy of LLR at Ex.R3 and 4.
In the cross-examination he admitted that as per Ex.R4 the driver Anjan holds LLR from 14.12.2022 to 13.06.2023.
Further he admitted that the said driver holds license to drive the LMV within the country.
However, the Respondent No.1 being the owner / driver of the offending vehicle did not appear before the Court and contested the matter to show the mode of the accident.
Further it is also worth to note here that the Respondent No.1 has not challenged Charge-sheet filed against him.
Hence, nothing elicited to contradict the claim of the Petitioner.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 by SCCH 15 13 MVC No.886/2023 its driver and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 34 years at the time of the accident.
The Petitioner has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P12, which shows his date of birth was 01.12.1988.
The accident taken place on 01.02.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 34 years and 2 months.
Hence, the age of the deceased, as on the date of accident was 35 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
18. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, he was running a Tailoring Shop and was earning 50,000/- per SCCH 15 14 MVC No.886/2023 month.
But, he has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
20.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-7 issued by the Medical Officer of the Ramaiah Hospital, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injury i.e.,
1) Swelling, tenderness and deformity with abnormal mobility over left arm at middle 1/3
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injury is grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
22.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 20,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
23. The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient.
Ex. P.15 - Case sheet of M.S. Ramaiah Hospital shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 01.02.2023 to 04.02.2023.
Therefore, while SCCH 15 16 MVC No.886/2023 calculating the total period of which the Petitioner admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 4 days.

sentences.text: Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 32,000/- under this head (@ 16,000/- per month ).

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
25.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 6,000/- (@ 100/- per day) towards attendants charges, 6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and 6,000/- towards conveyance would be just SCCH 15 17 MVC No.886/2023 and reasonable.

In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
26.
The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced medical bills and hospital bills at Ex.P9.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.1,25,193/-.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at 1,25,200/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for 1,25,200/- under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
27. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to do his work as he used to do earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. S.Ramachandra as PW.3 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by him at Ramaiah Hospital.
Further, he assessed the permanent residual physical disability of the Petitioner at 36.48% towards left upper limb and whole body disability at 12.16%.
PW.3 got marked Outpatient record and X-ray at Ex.P19 & 20.
In the cross- examination PW3 admitted that at present the Petitioner was walking without the external support.
Further he deposed that he has not seen the further treatment medical records of the Petitioner.
He also admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner was united.

He also admitted that Discharge summary does not show about the restrictions and the Petitioner had sustained simple fracture and he also admitted that he has not assessed the functional disability of the Petitioner.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.3 and the nature of the injuries sustained by SCCH 15 19 MVC No.886/2023 the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of Madan Kumar vs Anjan M.N on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380129/
7 the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 6% would be just and proper.
29. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 16.

With multiplier of 16, income of 16,000/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 6%, the loss of future income comes to 1,84,320/- (16,000/- x 12 = 1,92,000/-,
1,92,000/-x 16 x 6/100 = 1,84,320/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,84,320/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
30.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000 /-
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/-
 SCCH 15 20 MVC No.886/2023 3. Loss of income during the laid  32,000/-
 up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  18,000/-
 and conveyance 5. Medical expenses 1,25,200/-
6. Loss of Future Income 1,84,320/-
 Total 4,09,520/-
31.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 4,09,520/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

32. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
It is the main dispute of the Respondent No.2 that at the time of the accident the driver of the offending car did not possess valid Driving License.

On the other hand, the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner has vehemently argued that at the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.886/2023 time of the accident the driver of the offending vehicle holds LLR which is valid as on the date of accident.

Further he Madan Kumar vs Anjan M.N on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380129/
8 contended that the person who holds DL also sat by the side of the driver of the offending vehicle.

"Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, section 149(2)(a)(ii) and Central Motor Vehicles Rules,
1989, rules 3(1) and 24(3)(v) - Motor insurance - Driving license - Learner's licence - Liability of insurance company - pillion rider on motorcycle sustained fatal injuries due to negligence of the motorcyclist - insurance company disputes its liability on the ground that motorcyclist was possessing a learner's licence and according to rule 3(1)
motorcyclist was supposed to drive with an instructor - husband of the deceased pillion rider deposed that deceased was possessing license to drive motorcycle - no pleading or defence by insurance company that deceased was not holding a driving licence and that the travelled only as a pillion rider - Rule 24(3) (v) exempts a motorcyclist from the requirement of instructor to accompany - whether the Tribunal was justified the holding that learner's licence held by the motorcyclist was a valid licence and fastening liability on insurance company - Held: yes; motorcyclist need not be accompanied by an instructor."

There is no cogent evidence adduced by the Respondent No.2 to show that the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.886/2023 Respondent No.1 was not accompanied with the DL Holder by his side in the car at the time of accident.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that on the date of accident, the Respondent No.1 was accompanied with the DL holder by his side in the car.

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
33. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 25 MVC No.886/2023  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 4,09,520/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.
Due to which, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
He had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was running Tailoring shop and was earning 50,000/- per month.
On account of accidental injuries he cannot do his work.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 by its driver.
The Respondent SCCH 15 4 MVC No.886/2023 No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement contended that the Petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and SCCH 15 5 MVC No.886/2023 conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,84,320/- under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, the Respondent No.1 being the owner / driver of the offending vehicle did not appear before the Court and contested the matter to show the mode of the accident.
Hence, nothing elicited to contradict the claim of the Petitioner.
Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NF-2024 by SCCH 15 13 MVC No.886/2023 its driver and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
It is the main dispute of the Respondent No.2 that at the time of the accident the driver of the offending car did not possess valid Driving License.
It is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that the Respondent No.1 had driven the car without valid DL and has contravened the provisions of the MV Act and thereby committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
There is no cogent evidence adduced by the Respondent No.2 to show that the SCCH 15 24 MVC No.886/2023 Respondent No.1 was not accompanied with the DL Holder by his side in the car at the time of accident.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that on the date of accident, the Respondent No.1 was accompanied with the DL holder by his side in the car.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
SCCH 15 25 MVC No.886/2023  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 4,09,520/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
